(2) Consumer sweep: for each of G1's three named consumers I located the live consumer at be83ab65 (prune_jobs:3046, count_jobs_by_kind_status:2925 + deploy-server.md:266,273, stale_before_clause('updated_at') callers) and executed the round-4 predicate text against a sqlite3 fixture, then asked what the contract's own repair does to each. (3) Facility sweep: grepped crates/ at this tip for every statement-observation name, then located the facility on the deferred branch and read its recorder and its scoping to bound what 'enumerated from the LOG' can mean. (4) Vocabulary sweep: grep over crates/ and clients/ for every `== "completed"|"failed"|"cancelled"` compare AND every `JobStatus::<V>.to_string() ==` compare, then classified each as literal / enum-rendered / non-Rust / compiler-caught match arm, and separately located is_terminal, terminal_sql_list and non_terminal_sql_list callers. (5) Migration sweep: read 039's SQLite and Postgres constants and rustdoc in full, then ran three sqlite3 probes carrying 039's verbatim trigger text — ADD COLUMN/CREATE INDEX under the triggers, a non-canonical vs canonical stamped status UPDATE, and a table rebuild under foreign_keys=ON measuring both edges and triggers. Contract citations were checked one by one against be83ab65 with sed/grep. No cargo run and no Postgres lane was needed for any conclusion; every Postgres claim above is read from the committed SQL the backend renders (SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY, the sdchk__ CHECKs) rather than measured live.
